newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA ATTACKS AUSTRALIANS FOR SLEDGING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA ATTACKS AUSTRALIANS FOR SLEDGING.

text.p: West Indies vice-captain and star batsman Brian Lara criticised Australia for persistent sledging after scoring a century in the fifth and final test on Sunday.
Lara said the constant taunting and abuse by the Australians on the second day at the WACA Ground was unfortunate and unneccessary.
"The Australians have won the series and I think congratulations to them but they seem to be rubbing it in," Lara told reporters after close of play.

"They (the Australian players) talk a lot about 'losers' and stuff like that, well it's not necessary," said Lara, who scored 132 to lift his side's first innings total to 353 for seven, a lead of 110 runs.
Without identifying the culprits, Lara said he intervened after the Australians directed a stream of comments towards inexperienced opener Robert Samuels.
"I asked one of the guys to cool it a bit, he said 'it's no problem. I wouldn't say anything to you but to that loser up there....'
"They admonished a youngster (Samuels) who is trying his best. His test future is in a bit of a doubt. I was a bit disappointed with the Australian approach to him," Lara said.
At one point during his innings, Lara pointed his bat at Australia fast bowler Glenn McGrath while taking to his complaint to umpire Darrell Hair.
McGrath appeared to direct several comments to opener Samuels, who scored 76, his highest score of the test series.
At another point, Samuels appeared to poke out his tongue at Australian all-rounder Steve Waugh in a further exchange.
"The umpires did intervene and tried to calm things down but I don't think it was necessary to react in such a way especially after you win a series, Lara said."
Australia went into the fifth test with an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-test series.
"We are going to bounce back and we've got them in the Caribbean in two years' time. I promise you we will not be losing that series," Lara vowed.
